design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 0 (renters_billing_and_cancellation). Customer Delphine Okonkwo-Hallberg, RentGuard HO-4 Enhanced RG4-2417-3380, frozen_time 2026-09-13 11:20 EDT.

[0] Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6,4,6,5]. Assignment: discount-stop charge 6, discount-restart credit 6, late charge 4, catch-up amount 5.

[1] Why a good test. The caller asks one thing: pay by card, herself, whatever gets her account caught up after her September EFT bounced. The number she must be given (52.16) is not on any screen: the premium account is missing three owed postings, each with its own multi-factor calculation. A careless agent quotes the stored balance 40.77 or the ledger balance 38.39; a correct one reads four policies, discovers the umbrella that closed 2026-06-12 (discount stop owed), the floater that took effect 2026-08-20 (discount restart owed, but only after the stop is posted), the installment 7 unpaid past grace (late charge owed), posts them in order, then works the catch-up on the handling-time ledger. Difficulty comes from reading prerequisites, reconciling history across renters, umbrella, valuables and flood records, and arithmetic; there is one tool per action and no near-synonyms.

[2] Scope. Task 0 claims renters_ext_discount_stop_charge, renters_ext_discount_restart_credit, renters_ext_late_charge, renters_ext_catch_up_amount and tools post_discount_stop_charge_d8b9b7f1, post_discount_restart_credit_e779526e, assess_late_charge_664a192e, pay_catch_up_by_card_50a8e701 (user). Nothing was occupied before. Left for task 1: the whole ended-policy path (nonpayment cancellation cure and reinstatement fee), which none of these policies touches. Rejected scopes: anything writing renters_policy_cancelled (its umbrella trigger crosses category) and the rescission (no number to score).

[3] Problem tree (root renters_ext_catch_up_amount, on_request, owner=user tool).
 Edge 1: restart credit <- stop charge, value_input, gate restart_old_premium, form state. Sentence (negated direction, the way a credit desk states it): "The restart credit is not posted until the premium account carries a multi-policy discount change charge dated the closed date of every qualifying policy that ended earlier in the same renters term." Four-point test: ordering connective 'not ... until'; waits on a record-visible entry (additional premium, reason multi-policy discount change, dated the closed date); no tool/id/code token; scope 'every qualifying policy that ended earlier in the same renters term' = the condition. Exactly one write of the difficulty books that entry (post_discount_stop_charge_d8b9b7f1). Derivation: sentence + umbrella closed_date 2026-06-12 + no such entry on the account + the stop policy's rule ('posted as one additional premium entry with change_reason multi_policy_discount_change dated the closed date of the ending qualifying policy') -> post the stop charge. False at opening: umbrella_policies.closed_date=2026-06-12, 22 billing entries none of them additional premium, term_premium=237.24. Deletion run: restart credit 16.31 instead of 17.57.
 Edge 2: catch-up <- restart credit, value_input, gate catch_balance, form state, affirmative ('is fixed only after'): waits on a return premium entry, multi-policy discount change, dated each new qualifying policy's effective date; only post_discount_restart_credit_e779526e books it. False at opening: valuables_floaters.effective_date=2026-08-20, no return premium entry. Deletion run: catch-up 69.73 instead of 52.16.
 Edge 3: catch-up <- late charge, value_input, gate catch_balance, form state: waits on 'each installment of the term left unpaid past its late-fee grace period carries a late charge on the premium account'; only assess_late_charge_664a192e books fee_code late_fee. False at opening: installment 7 due 2026-09-01, its payment returned 2026-09-04, no late fee entry. Deletion run: catch-up 25.81 (balance 6.58 lower and nothing is collected ahead of billing).
 value_input edges: 3 >= max(3-1,1)=2. Topological order: stop -> restart -> late -> catch-up. The late charge commutes with both discount postings (no shared input): replaying late -> stop -> restart -> catch-up gives 6.58, 8.61, 17.57, 52.16 and an identical terminal hash (t0_order check). user_scenario names none of these problems. The tools validate nothing: each reads the policy row only to copy customer_id and the balance and writes what it is given.

[4] Factor cards (tier taken; evidence; baseline figure of result from the sensitivity run; every figure re-checked for half-cent ties).
 Stop charge 8.61 (baseline all factors 13.24): courtesy period (method, anchor) umbrella insured_request, held 29 months -> 262-30=232 days [9.84]; plan proration (method, day-count) monthly_eft -> 7 whole 30-day periods /12 [9.38]; flood relief (parameter, cross-difficulty flood, multi-source) FloodGuard FG-2356-0418 in force at the same address, 2 payments in 24 months -> 20 [10.76]; tenure relief 42 months -> 5 [9.15]; claim-record relief claim reported 2023-11-02, no payment in 36 months -> 5 [9.15]; dishonour points one return -> 10 subtracted [7.53]. Near-miss: the 2024-05-09 flood payment is outside 24 months; the umbrella's current-term effective date 2026-01-15 is not its bound date; the floater is in force and is not an ending policy.
 Restart credit 17.57 (baseline 9.76): start date (method, anchor) floater bound 2026-08-01, 19 days ahead, annual plan -> from bound date, 212 days [15.38]; proration (method) monthly_eft, part period counted whole -> 8/12 [15.31]; schedule points 12,500 -> 1 [15.81]; household points (cross-difficulty flood, multi-source) FloodGuard 28 months -> 2 [14.06]; tenure points 42 months -> 1 [15.81]; dishonour points one return -> 1 subtracted [19.33].
 Late charge 6.58 (baseline 5.00): tenure base (multi-source) 42 months and no late charge in 12 months -> 3.00 [8.58]; dishonour addition one return -> 1.00 [5.58]; installment size 19.77+1.00=20.77 -> 0.50 [6.08]; lateness method (method: flat / flat plus percentage / percentage only) 12 days -> combined 4.50 + 10% of 20.77 = 6.577 [4.50]. Near-miss: the returned-payment fee 20.00 is a fee but not a late charge.
 Catch-up 52.16 (baseline 38.39): collection ahead of billing (method: unbilled term premium / next installment with its service charge / nothing) one return and a late charge in 12 months -> next installment 19.77 + 1.00 [32.39]; early service charge relief 42 months -> 1.00 waived [53.16]; prompt credit 9 days after the return on monthly_eft -> 5.00 [57.16]; card service charge no card payment in 12 months -> 2.00 [50.16]; flood household credit (cross-difficulty flood) annual plan paid 2026-05-07 -> 3.00 [55.16]. Near-miss: premium_balance shows 40.77 (the stale figure the customer quotes); the ledger after the postings gives 38.39.

[5] Base invariants. Stop/restart: renters_agg_bundle_discount, renters_midterm_changes, renters_insured_cancellation, renters_reinstatement govern the additional/return premium subjects; none has a gate applying to these events (changeable_status applies to relocation/coverage updates) so all enter as policy_scope; policy in force. Overrides declared: midterm proration sentence and bundle start/stop sentence (both), premium-rating discount sentence (restart). Late charge: renters_fees_and_waivers.late_fee_grace (time): anchor renters_billing.due_date 2026-09-01, calendar days, exclusive, 10 days -> posting allowed from 2026-09-12; 2026-09-11 would fail, 2026-09-13 passes. The tier amount 5.00 is not 0.00 so a charge is due. Catch-up: renters_payment_application, no gate on payment received.

[6] Business objects. Stop charge: the one umbrella (closed 2026-06-12) and the renters term 2026-03-01..2027-03-01. Restart: the one floater effective 2026-08-20. Late charge: installment 7 (term 2026-03-01, number 7), keyed by term_effective_date + installment_number; installments 1-6 paid by EFT on their due dates and excluded. Catch-up: every renters billing entry of the policy (22 seeded + 3 posted); flood payments counted only through the flood policy of this customer.

[7] Seed. customers 1; renters_policies 1 (term premium 237.24 = 263.60 less 10 percent, balance 40.77 = ledger); renters_billing 22 (7 installments of 19.77, 6 EFT service charges 1.00, 7 EFT payments, 1 return 20.77 on 2026-09-04, 1 returned-payment fee 20.00); renters_claims 3 (claim RGC-23-204417 reported/denied/closed 2023-11); umbrella 1 (cancelled, insured_request); valuables 1 (in force); flood 1 + flood_billing 6 (three annual bills of 170.00 and payments). Automatic clauses checked: installment 8 posts 2026-09-16 (after frozen_time); nonpayment notice would be allowed only from 2026-09-14; returned payments 1 < limit 2 (no EFT suspension); no renewal event within the window.

[8] Persona. Brisk scheduler; opening = bounced September payment + pay by card whatever it takes; identity (phone, DOB) and policy number only when asked; other policies only when asked, as plain holdings; accepts any explanation without numbers; pays exactly the handed-over amount; ends on the confirmation. The only figure she holds is the app's 40.77 (premium_balance at the opening).

[9] Standard solution. find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, DOB) -> read policy, premium account, claims, umbrella, floater, flood policy, flood billing -> stop charge (policy, 2026-06-12, 255.69, 8.61) -> restart credit (policy, 2026-08-20, 229.33, 17.57) -> late charge (policy, 2026-03-01, 7, 6.58) -> hand over and the customer pays 52.16.

[10] Verification actually run (scratch builder using the gate's own evaluator on the replayed handling-time DB): stop 8.61, restart 17.57, late 6.58, catch-up 52.16; skip-runs 16.31 / 69.73 / 25.81; gates check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks (17 actions, det True, closure 36/36), check_solvability (4 calls, 9 base gates, 26 seed rows), check_compute (21 factors, 3 cross-difficulty, 37 history rows, 86 branches after round 2), check_grounding, check_cross_fire all OK for --task 0.

[11] Draft recomputation from the visible context. From the published rules, tool schemas, lookups and the persona alone: the rules of the four policies each name their own records; the restart credit's sentence and the catch-up's two sentences reveal that three postings are owed; the lookups show the umbrella closed, the floater started, installment 7 returned; the arithmetic above follows sentence by sentence. The one judgement not mechanical — that the late charge and the discount postings may be in either order — is harmless because they commute.

[12] Revisions. (a) Symptom: check_extended flagged helper '_policy' as an unnamed tool and as a tool name inside rules. Root cause: a module-level helper counted as a tool function. Change: inlined the policy lookup in every tool. Re-run: EXTENDED OK. (b) Removed a no-op ternary from catch_days_since_return before the first compute run.

[13] Revision round 2 (policy-task audit, revision_0 -> revision_1), item by item.
 F-1 / F-T0-1 (undeclared late-fee override): renters_ext_late_charge now declares an overwrite of renters_fees_and_waivers "The returned-payment fee is charged once per returned payment, referencing that return, and the reinstatement fee once per reinstatement; a fee whose tier amount is 0.00 is not charged at all." replaced by the rule sentence that keeps both other fees and the 0.00 exemption and states that a late fee is charged at the late charge worked out, not at the tier's late_fee alone. No gate condition is quoted, so late_fee_grace stays inherited. The base reading (5.00) is now excluded by a declared override.
 F-2 (late_lateness_scaling mislabelled): replaced by late_lateness_method, whose tiers select three different algorithms (percentage-only charge after 30 days; flat base with additions plus 10 percent of the unpaid part at 12-30 days; flat charge before 12 days). Late charge 6.75 -> 6.58; catch-up follows.
 F-3 (catch_acceleration mislabelled) and O-FL2 (accelerated service charge baseline not stated): replaced by catch_ahead_of_billing (method: unbilled term premium computed as annual premium less billed installments / next installment plus the plan's service charge / nothing) and catch_early_service_charge_relief (parameter, baseline 0 = nothing waived), so every factor's fall-through is what baseline.rule states. Catch-up -> 52.16.
 F-T0-3 (false proof figure 9.22, half-cent tie): the float evaluator rounds an exact .xx5 tie down. Changed flood_relief_full_pct 25 -> 20 so that neither gold nor any sensitivity lands on a tie (stop 18.45 x 7/12 x 0.80 = 8.61 exactly; courtesy baseline 9.84; every rounding checked with a tie detector: none). Stop 8.07 -> 8.61.
 O-RC1: rule now says the ending qualifying policy is the one with the latest closed date; compute takes max(umbrella closed, floater closed) and reads reason and bound date from that policy. O-RC2/O-RC3: the overdue installment is the latest billed whose due date is already past (compute steps back one installment when the latest billed is not yet due) and its service charge is the one billed with that same installment. O-T0-1: the late rule states that an installment whose payment was returned is unpaid from its due date. O-RC5/O-OV2: stop and restart rules state that the pre-discount premium is taken from the current premium by division, not rebuilt, including a premium held at the minimum. O-PG1: restart edge condition trimmed to the sentence's strength. O-PS1: the catch-up's restart sentence now covers only qualifying policies that took effect while the premium carried no multi-policy discount (the only case the restart rule credits). O-OV3: the catch-up rule states that what the payment carries beyond the balance stays as a credit toward the next charges. O-FL1: restart tier 2 now counts from 7 days before the new policy's effective date, never before the renters effective date (no days beyond expiration). O-FL3: relief/points kept (no tier outcome identified as unpublishable); recorded. O-RC4: no change needed.
 Re-run after the revision: see [10]; all gates green.
user_scenario: You are Delphine Okonkwo-Hallberg, a 36-year-old surgical scheduling coordinator in Columbus who rents an apartment at 2291 Northwest Boulevard, Apt 3C, and keeps her whole life in spreadsheets. You are calling Larkspur Mutual on your lunch break because your bank bounced the automatic payment for your renters insurance at the start of September; you had moved money between accounts and the draft hit the empty one. You open with something like: "My bank bounced my September renters payment and I want to get my account completely caught up today. I'll pay by card right now, whatever it takes." You want it settled in this one call. You are happy for the representative to post whatever their own records need on the account, but the payment itself you want to make yourself with your own debit card. Your banking app's insurance summary showed about forty dollars owing, $40.77, and that is the only figure you have in mind; you have no idea how Larkspur works anything out. When the representative asks you to confirm who you are, you give your phone number, 330-218-4467, and your date of birth, July 23, 1990 (1990-07-23); if they want one more detail you add your email, delphine.okhallberg@fastmail.com, or your ZIP code, 43214. Your renters policy number, RG4-2417-3380, you read off your insurance card only if asked. If the representative asks about your other Larkspur policies, you answer plainly: you cancelled your personal umbrella in June because you no longer needed it, you took out a Valuables Floater in August for your engagement ring, and you have a small flood policy on your belongings in the apartment; you don't remember dates or amounts beyond that and tell them to look them up. If the representative says something on the account has to be put right on their side, you say that's fine and to go ahead, without asking for details. When they tell you the amount to pay and it isn't the forty dollars you expected, you ask once, calmly, why it's different; whatever the explanation, you accept it and never offer numbers of your own. Once the representative hands the payment over to you, you make the card payment on your policy for exactly the amount they gave you. When the payment goes through and you have the confirmation number, you read it back, thank them and end the call. If they tell you the account is all set without ever handing you a payment to make, you thank them and hang up.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.renters_policy_id: 77d033e2-ff0b-4f80-9556-dd8210849a8b. Basis: the renters policy lookup returns exactly one RentGuard policy (RG4-2417-3380) for customer 0336f8b9-346b-46af-928d-55c41cd30c5d; the docstring asks for 'the reference number of the RentGuard renters policy record being charged'. Uniqueness: the customer holds no other renters policy.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.effective_date: 2026-06-12. Basis: the rule says the charge is 'dated the closed date of the ending qualifying policy'; the umbrella lookup shows closed_date 2026-06-12 and it is the only qualifying policy that ended, so it is the one with the latest closed date. Uniqueness: the courtesy period changes only the days charged, never the entry's date; the floater is in force and cannot be the ending policy.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.restated_term_premium: 255.69. Basis: 'The annual premium after the stop is the annual premium before discounts reduced by autopay_discount_pct when the billing plan is monthly_eft and by no other percentage ... and it is restated'. 237.24 / (1 - (3 + 7)/100) = 263.60; 263.60 x 0.97 = 255.692 -> 255.69 (above the 149.00 minimum). Uniqueness: the plan is monthly_eft (autopay 3 kept), the umbrella was the only qualifying policy, so no other percentage survives.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 8.61. Factors: annual change 255.69 - 237.24 = 18.45; stop courtesy period: the umbrella is the only (and so the latest-closed) qualifying policy that ended in the term, cancelled at insured request after 29 months held -> days charged DAYS(2026-06-12, 2027-03-01) - 30 = 262 - 30 = 232; stop proration: monthly_eft -> int(232/30) = 7 whole periods / 12; flood relief: FloodGuard in force at 2291 Northwest Boulevard, Apt 3C with 2 payments in 24 months -> 20; tenure relief: 42 months -> 5; claim-record relief: claim reported 2023-11-02, no payment in 36 months -> 5; dishonour points: one return (2026-09-04) in 12 months -> 10 subtracted; relief 20+5+5-10 = 20. 18.45 x 7/12 x 0.80 = 8.61, above min_premium_change 2.00.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden task tool post_discount_restart_credit_e779526e so it can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the discount-restart credit; no DB effect, unlocked once.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Post the discount-restart credit of 17.57 dated 2026-08-20 and restate the annual premium to 229.33.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: renters_ext_discount_restart_credit uniquely produces amount 17.57 from the restated premium left by the stop charge.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.renters_policy_id: 77d033e2-ff0b-4f80-9556-dd8210849a8b. Basis: the same single RentGuard policy RG4-2417-3380 returned by the renters policy lookup. Uniqueness: no other renters policy exists for the customer.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.effective_date: 2026-08-20. Basis: the credit is 'dated the effective date of the new qualifying policy'; the floater lookup shows effective_date 2026-08-20. Uniqueness: the start-date factor moves only the days credited (from the bound date 2026-08-01), not the entry date.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.restated_term_premium: 229.33. Basis: 'The annual premium after the restart is the annual premium without discounts reduced by the discount percentages after the restart ... and it is restated'. Current premium after the stop 255.69 / 0.97 = 263.5979 -> 263.60; percentages: autopay 3 + multi-policy 7 + schedule points 1 (12,500 scheduled) + household points 2 (FloodGuard 28 months) + tenure points 1 (42 months) - dishonour points 1 (one return) = 13; 263.60 x 0.87 = 229.332 -> 229.33.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 17.57. Factors: annual reduction 255.69 - 229.33 = 26.36; restart start date: floater bound 2026-08-01, 19 days before it took effect, annual plan -> days credited DAYS(2026-08-01, 2027-03-01) = 212; restart proration: monthly_eft -> 212/30 = 7.07, part period counted whole -> 8 / 12 = 0.666667; 26.36 x 0.666667 = 17.5733 -> 17.57. Handling time: evaluated after the stop charge restated the premium to 255.69 (from 237.24 the credit would be 16.31).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden task tool assess_late_charge_664a192e so it can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the late charge on installment 7; no DB effect, unlocked once.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.renters_policy_id: 77d033e2-ff0b-4f80-9556-dd8210849a8b. Basis: the single RentGuard policy of the customer. Uniqueness: no other renters policy.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.term_effective_date: 2026-03-01. argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 6.58. Factors: late charge base by tenure: 42 months and no late charge in 12 months -> 3.00 (tier late fee would be 5.00); dishonour addition: one return in 12 months -> 1.00; installment size: 19.77 + the service charge billed with it 1.00 = 20.77 -> 0.50; lateness method: DAYS(2026-09-01, 2026-09-13) = 12 -> combined charge: (3.00 + 1.00 + 0.50) + 10 percent of 20.77 = 4.50 + 2.077 = 6.577 -> 6.58.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 52.16. Factors: account balance reconciled from the ledger after the three postings: 40.77 + 8.61 - 17.57 + 6.58 = 38.39; collection ahead of billing: exactly one return in 12 months and a late charge now posted -> the next scheduled installment 19.77 plus the monthly_eft service charge 1.00 = 20.77; service charge relief: 42 months -> the 1.00 is waived; prompt credit: 9 days since the 2026-09-04 return (<= 10 grace days) on monthly_eft -> 5.00 off; card service charge: no card payment in 12 months -> installment_fee_card 2.00 added; flood household credit: FloodGuard on the annual plan paid 2026-05-07 -> 3.00 off. 38.39 + 20.77 - 1.00 + 2.00 - 5.00 - 3.00 = 52.16.

stop_tenure_relief (parameter): original effective 2023-03-01 -> 42 months -> 5 points; baseline 0 -> result 9.15.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The stop charge must precede the restart credit (the restart credit's prerequisite sentence; value 17.57 after it, 16.31 without it). The late charge commutes with both discount postings: it reads only installments, installment service charges, late fees, returned payments, tenure and today's date, none of which a discount posting writes, and the discount postings read returned payments, installment counts, holdings and the term premium, none of which the late charge writes. Replaying the order late charge -> stop -> restart -> catch-up gives the same four amounts (6.58, 8.61, 17.57, 52.16) and the same terminal DB hash as the gold order (checked by replay: see design_rationale).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the stop charge leaves term_premium at 237.24, so the restart credit recomputes to 16.31 instead of 17.57 (and the terminal account lacks the 8.61 charge).
Skipping the restart credit leaves the account balance 17.57 higher: the catch-up recomputes to 69.73 instead of 52.16.
Skipping the late charge lowers the balance by 6.58 and, with no late charge in 12 months, nothing is collected ahead of billing: the catch-up recomputes to 25.81 instead of 52.16.
